answers.q: What drives you nuts?
a: Bad comms.
Bad documentation. Scaling is a context-sharing problem.
Not making decisions.
Inconsistent branding.
When someone says “Let's A/B test it!”

answers.q: What are your quirks?
a: I (sometimes) use the third person. Someone even got t-shirts made.
I have infinite energy for work but I must work out and eat healthy, or my energy goes to zero in 24 to 48 hours.

answers.q: How can people earn an extra gold star with you?
a: Be thoughtful about comms.
Invite me for a coffee run or a walk.
Let's go skiing.

answers.q: What qualities do you particularly value in people who work with you?
a: Low ego.
High agency.
High output.
Great async comms.
Taste.
Honest feedback.
Decisiveness.

answers.q: What are some things that people might misunderstand about you?
a: If I come in guns blazing it's because I want to get stuff done, sometimes at the expense of other things.

answers.q: How do you coach people to do their best work and develop their talents?
a: I ask questions to understand where you're going and, if you don't know, help you figure that out.
I provide clear expectations and ambitious goals, and give you the tools to reach them.
I have your best interest in mind. If the best place for you is outside the org, I'm going to say so.

answers.q: What's the best way to communicate with you?
a: A thoughtful async message: Slack, or a memo.
Give me a call. I'll usually walk my dogs.

answers.q: What's the best way to convince you to do something?
a: I don't need convincing. If you asked me to do X, I'll assume you thought through the alternatives.
That said, providing reasoning helps. I don't need data, but it helps to understand where your conviction is coming from.

answers.q: How do you like to give feedback?
a: I adjust to the other person's style if it's stated explicitly.
Otherwise a thoughtful message with examples, then a call to chat it through.
I tend to give more constructive criticism than positive feedback. Trying to update that.

answers.q: How do you like to get feedback?
a: Slight preference for async first, then live. Can also do live. But please don't be vague.

people.values: Optimism, at a micro level (life will be OK) and a macro level (technology will save the world). Honesty: radical honesty, not for others but for myself. Default to trust. Positive sum: build a bigger pie. Progressive progress: as long as I'm better today than yesterday, I'll take it.

answers.q: What are some honest, unfiltered things about you?
a: Enneagram: tied for a 6 (The Loyalist) and an 8 (The Challenger).
Six: I create order out of chaos, I like being part of something greater than myself, and I give 110% when I commit.
Eight: highly independent, I see potential in people, and when I say I'm going to do something I do it.

answers.q: What drives you nuts?
a: Little things: consistent small noises.
Big things: when people do not engage with others in a thoughtful and respectful way.

answers.q: How can people earn an extra gold star with you?
a: Be super transparent and forthcoming. I want to help, and I operate better with full context.
Share the big unfiltered ideas. Push yourself and others to think outside the box.

answers.q: What qualities do you particularly value in people who work with you?
a: Adjusting your approach to the person in front of you. Not everyone works or takes in information the same way.
Desire to improve: taking feedback in stride, going out of your way to get it, acknowledging your own missteps.
Being human.

answers.q: What are some things that people might misunderstand about you?
a: I've heard I can come across as intimidating, likely because I'm very direct and not afraid of hard conversations. I do it from a place of care and wanting what's best for people.

answers.q: How do you coach people to do their best work and develop their talents?
a: Meet people where they are. I try to understand where they're trying to go and what's actually in the way.
The GROW model has worked well for people I've managed and coached.

answers.q: What's the best way to communicate with you?
a: Small things: Slack or text.
Big things: call me, Zoom, or in person.

answers.q: What's the best way to convince you to do something?
a: Just ask. If there's a reason you think I won't want to do it, tee it up and then give me a call.

answers.q: How do you like to give feedback?
a: Prefer a live conversation, but I'll give feedback in whatever format works best for the person receiving it.

answers.q: How do you like to get feedback?
a: Live conversation.

people.values: Understand the human in front of you: take the time to understand what makes them tick and the life experiences that shaped their worldview. Be transparent and direct, but never disrespectful. Be bold and adaptive: don't do things just because that's how they've been done. Get back up: have your down moments, then get back up.
